holidays.name: National Vanilla Ice Cream Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the world's most popular ice cream flavor, which is somehow also the word people use to describe anything bland. Grab a scoop, add sprinkles, and prove that vanilla is anything but boring.
holidays.origin: July is National Ice Cream Month, a designation made by President Ronald Reagan in 1984. Vanilla Ice Cream Day is an unofficial food holiday that grew out of that celebration and is observed on different dates in different places, including July 23.
holidays.funFact: Vanilla comes from orchid pods and is the second most expensive spice in the world after saffron. Each vanilla flower must be pollinated by hand outside its native Mexico.

holidays.name: National Hot Dog Day (Unofficial Observance Window)
holidays.description: A day for dedicating yourself to the glory of the humble frankfurter, with endless debate about ketchup, mustard, and whether a hot dog is a sandwich.
holidays.origin: The National Hot Dog and Sausage Council promotes hot dog celebrations throughout July, which is National Hot Dog Month, and different hot dog days are observed across the summer.
holidays.funFact: Americans eat an estimated 20 billion hot dogs a year, which works out to roughly 70 per person.

holidays.name: Gorgeous Grandma Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating grandmothers who are fabulous, stylish, and full of sass. It is an excuse to tell Grandma she looks great and ask for the secret family recipes.
holidays.origin: An unofficial, feel-good observance that is celebrated on July 23 in the United States to honor grandmothers.
holidays.funFact: Studies of family life have found that grandparents are often among the most important sources of childcare in many countries, giving the day extra meaning.

holidays.name: Hot Dog Day... Not! It's Penuche Fudge Day
holidays.description: A sweet day for honoring penuche, a creamy brown sugar fudge with a caramel-like flavor. It is the fudge for people who think chocolate gets too much attention.
holidays.origin: National Penuche Fudge Day is an unofficial food holiday observed on July 23. Penuche is a New England classic made from brown sugar, butter, and milk.
holidays.funFact: Penuche is believed to take its name from the Spanish word 'panocha,' a type of raw sugar, and it is notoriously tricky to make because it can turn grainy if stirred at the wrong time.

holidays.name: Fry Day Eve... National Sprinkles Day Neighbor: Hot Enough For Ya Day
holidays.description: A cheeky observance of sweltering midsummer weather, when everyone feels obliged to ask 'Hot enough for you?' Participants are encouraged to answer with a creative, heat-themed comeback.
holidays.origin: This is a humorous, informal tradition rooted in the peak of summer heat in the Northern Hemisphere, where late July is often the hottest stretch of the year.
holidays.funFact: Late July is typically the hottest time of the year across much of the Northern Hemisphere, and the highest temperature ever reliably recorded on Earth, 134°F (56.7°C) in Death Valley, occurred on July 10, 1913.
